title: The Interchange Between Bible and Archaeology: The Case of David's Palace and the Millo
author: Nadav Na'aman
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted magazine article (peer-adjacent BAR feature by an academic historian). Project stores its own summary of the proposal only; no reproduction of the article's text or images.
summary: Na'aman, a historian of the ancient Near East, argues for identifying the biblical Millo (2 Samuel 5:9, 'built the city all around from the Millo inward') with the excavated Stepped Stone Structure on the City of David's northeastern slope -- the massive stone-and-earth terrace system Eilat Mazar's excavations describe as supporting the 'Large Stone Structure' above it (mazar-2009-palace-of-king-david). Na'aman reads the name Millo (from a Hebrew root meaning 'to fill') as a natural fit for a constructed terrace/fill system of exactly this kind, and treats the identification as a case study in how a specific archaeological feature and a specific textual reference can be responsibly interchanged. This project cites Na'aman as the named proponent of the terrace/stepped-structure identification of the Millo on claim-millo-identification's 'excavated stepped-stone/terrace structure' scholarlyView -- it does not adopt the identification, since the dating of the relevant construction phase (whether any phase is as early as David's reign) remains independently disputed (see mazar-2005-chronology and the finkelstein-herzog-singer-avitz-ussishkin-2007-tel-aviv rebuttal of the adjoining Large Stone Structure's dating).
